children: Shares in Boohoo climbed after the company said it sold its Sheffield distribution center, which will now be leased by Primark.
The company, which has rebranded as Debenhams Group, said Thursday that it sold the warehouse and reassigned the lease to Primark for a consideration of 90 million pounds in cash, or $121.9 million.
Boohoo's stock was up around 11% at 23.50 pence in European morning trading.
"The Debenhams Group turnaround continues at pace, and this transaction helps accelerate our progress," Chief Executive Dan Finley said.
As a result of the disposal, Boohoo now expects net debt to be negligible at the end of fiscal 2027, which runs through February.

"We view this as a transformational deal, which has now taken any debt concerns off the table," Peel Hunt analysts John Stevenson and Jonathan Pritchard wrote in a note. The recovery seems to be gaining traction, they added.

The company also reported an acceleration in gross merchandise value growth in the second quarter. Earlier this year, Boohoo said it expected the metric to return to year-on-year growth in fiscal 2027.
Gross merchandise value is a key industry metric that refers to the total value of all transactions made on the platform.
The group will provide a trading update for the first half on Sept. 17.
